courses.title: Ultimate Questions: An Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: [GE 3B] Investigation into the big questions of philosophy (Does God Exist? Can I Know Anything? Who Am I? How Should I Live? Am I Free); emphasis on how philosophers propose to answer such questions and their relevance for intelligent living.

courses.title: Ethical Problems in Contemporary Life
courses.description: [GE 3B] Investigation and application of central theoretical traditions in philosophical ethics. Analysis and appraisal of ethical arguments. Development of ethical reasoning skills. Critical consideration of controversial topics in personal, professional, social, and global ethics.

courses.title: Logic and Computing
courses.description: [GE 2] Cross Listed as: CS 2180 Introduction to formal techniques for analyzing and evaluating natural language arguments; discussion of relation between these formal techniques and computer gates and computer programming.

courses.title: Philosophy Proseminar II: Philosophical Methods
courses.description: Develops skills necessary for proficiency in philosophical reading, research, and written and oral presentation.

courses.title: Moral Philosophy
courses.description: Investigation of central traditions in moral theory, including utilitarianism, virtue theory, Kantianism, contract theories, feminism. Inquiry into the justification and implications of moral principles and claims. Analysis of moral obligation, interests, happiness. Skeptical challenge to morality’s presumed authority.
courses.prerequisites: PHL 201, PHL 2010 , PHL 204, or PHL 2040 ; or instructor permission.

courses.title: Epistemology
courses.description: An investigation into the nature, scope, and limits of human knowledge. Survey of major topics such as foundationalism, coherentism, reliabilism contextualism and skepticism.

courses.title: Senior Seminar in Philosophy
courses.description: Development and writing of a thesis in philosophy on the basis of extensive research. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Philosophy and Religion of Japan
courses.description: “Traditional ways of thought in Japan. Modifications from its beginnings through the impacts of Buddhism and Confucianism; its reemergence in the 19th Century. Twentieth-century developments and the emergence of the “”New Religions”“. ”

courses.title: Philosophy and Religion of China
courses.description: Development of religious thought in China with special reference to Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhist schools of thought.

courses.title: Philosophy and Religion of India
courses.description: The diversity of the philosophy and religion of India from Rig Vedic times to the 20th Century. Development of the Upanishads, Yoga systems, the great epics, the Bhakti movements; Emergence of Jainism, Buddhism, Sikhism, Indian Islam.

courses.title: Philosophy of Asian Martial Arts and Religion
courses.description: Examination of various styles of Asian martial arts and meditation, and of the philosophical traditions from which they have developed. Emphasizes both theory and practice. 3 hours lecture/discussion

courses.title: Feminist Philosophy
courses.description: Examination of several of the central metaphysical, epistemological, ethical, social, and political questions in Feminist Philosophy. Topics include theories of gender difference, including social construction, realism, and new essentialisms; the relations between sex and gender; feminist epistemologies, including feminist perspectives on objectivity in science, feminist critiques of scientific practice, epistemologies of ignorance, standpoint epistemology, epistemic injustice, and the relations between knowledge and emotion; misrepresenting women, gendered narrative, and women’s appearance; intersectionality and the interactions among gender, race, class, sexuality, immigration status, ability and other social categories; structural injustice, including global gender injustice, transnational feminism, and individual bias; gender and work, including family and domestic work, sex work, and reproductive freedom and abortion; and theorizing misogyny, policing women, and domestic violence.

courses.title: Comparative Philosophy
courses.description: A comparative study of Eastern philosophy and Western philosophy. The study will include metaphysics, epistemology, methodology and socio-political values and ideals. Designed for strong interest in multicultural studies.

courses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy
courses.description: Examination of the philosophical ideas of the Greek and Roman worlds, from the pre-Socratic philosophers to the Hellenistic schools. Critical investigation of metaphysical, epistemological and ethical disputes among ancient thinkers.

courses.title: Great Works in Philosophy
courses.description: Study in depth of a historically significant work of philosophy with attention devoted to primary source materials. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 6 units.
courses.prerequisites: Any upper division course with PHL prefix.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.title: History of Modern Philosophy
courses.description: Great philosophical ideas and thinkers from Galileo to Kant.

courses.title: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Examination of problems in the philosophy of mind including knowledge of other minds, and the nature of mental states and their properties, in particular, consciousness and representation.

courses.title: Metaphysics
courses.description: Fundamental problems that have been central to philosophy throughout its history: substance and attributes, identity and change, personal identity, causality, determinism, free will, and the nature of time.

courses.title: Existentialism
courses.description: Basic ideas of existentialist philosophers of the 19th and 20th centuries; a comparison of theistic and atheistic existentialism; existentialist ideas of anxiety, freedom, and responsibility.

courses.title: Seminar in Law and Values
courses.description: Investigation of a central area of inquiry in moral, political, or legal philosophy, with special emphasis on contemporary texts and thinkers. Content varies as offered. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: PHL 3090 , PHL 3100 , PHL 3110 , or consent of instructor; and junior or senior standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken unlimited times only with different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Metaphysics and Epistemology
courses.description: Examination of central controversies or recent developments in the areas of metaphysics, philosophy of language, philosophy of mind, or epistemology, with special emphasis on contemporary texts and thinkers. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: PHL 3590 , PHL 3600 , or consent of instructor; and junior or senior standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: May be repeated for credit for a maximum of 6 units.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
